findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was only able to produce one signed employee reporting agreement during today’s inspection. A blank copy of the SCDPH Employee Reporting Agreement was provided to the PIC. All employees handling food or drinks to be served to the public must read and sign employee reporting agreements, which symptoms associated with common food-borne illnesses. This agreement also advises on restriction and exclusion requirements. Ensure all employees read and sign the report by 10/15/25, and retain these agreements on file for future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink at the upstairs satellite bar to not have paper towels. CORRECTED- the PIC placed some napkins upstairs for hand drying. Ensure all sinks used for hand washing always have warm running water, soap, and paper towels available.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a slight accumulation of soil debris on the interior of the ice machine located in the facility’s basement. Food contact surfaces should be maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of foods (ice). Ensure ice machine is emptied and the interior is cleaned and sanitized by 10/15/25.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two opened containers of creamer without date marking. CORRECTED- the PIC knew when the creamer downstairs was opened and placed the corresponding date on the container. The creamer upstairs was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with their opening date if held for more than one day. Use or discard TCS items within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector and PIC observed multiple ants on the soda nozzle in the upstairs satellite bar. CORRECTED- the PIC cleaned and sanitized the soda nozzle, and stated that it should have been soaking. Ensure pest control is obtained (or verified) and monitored to prevent the contamination of drinks and garnishes.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed neither of the upstairs bathroom doors to contain self-closers. Provide self closers on all restroom doors to prevent the contamination of potable beverages.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: (SECOND REPEAT) Inspector observed the floor at the back walk-in-cooler to contain spots of bare wood, as well as chipping into the surface of the floor near the door. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Wood is highly absorbent and may allow for the entry and harborage of mold. Seal or repair floors by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers certificates during today’s inspection. All employees who handle food or drinks must obtain a Food Handlers card; and renew it every three years. Course completion reviews safe food handling practices and cold holding temperatures, among other important food safety standards. Ensure all bar tenders obtain a Food Handlers certificate, and maintain a copy on file to be made available during future routine inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Signed reporting agreements were not available during this inspection. CORRECTED- Staff present signed agreements. Ensure signed reporting agreements are on file for all employees who handle food or ice.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
One soda nozzle at the main bar observed soiled with mold accumulation. CORRECTED- Soda gun was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. Maintain clean to sight and touch.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
Both upstairs restroom doors are not self-closing. Provide self closers on both restroom doors.
6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floor of the large walk-in cooler was observed with chipped flooring near the door and in a few spots within the cooler. Repair the floor in the walk-in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Both ice machines had flecks of black debris that appeared to be mold in and on the ice cubes. Ice machines were just fully serviced by a local company 2 weeks ago. Manager contacted the company during inspection to advise of the issue and request additional service. Both ice machines were shut off during inspection. Ice will be discarded, and both ice machines will be cleaned and sanitized prior to use the next day of operation. **See General Comments for additional information**
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 The 3 part sink at the bar on the main floor has two faucets. The faucet fixture on the left side of the sink is loose, and the cold water handle could not be turned. A plumber has already been contacted to get the fixture replaced. Manager will check with the plumber regarding parts. In the meantime, the faucet fixture on the right is working properly and was observed with both hot and cold running water to allow for proper temperature control of water during ware washing.
-Right handwashing sink in the women’s restroom on the main floor is currently out of service. One of the handles got torn off over the weekend, and the water lines were shut off to the sink. Owner has been in touch with the plumber. Service is scheduled to occur later this week. In the meantime, the left handwashing sink was observed properly stocked with both hot and cold water available during the inspection. Owner was advised to post a sign indicating the right sink was temporarily out of order to discourage potential attempts at using it.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
5-501.17 Covered waste receptacles were available in the women’s restroom on the second floor but were missing from the women’s restroom on the main floor of the facility. Provide covered waste receptacles for the women’s restroom on the main floor.
Women's room did not have a covered waste receptacle. Provide at least one covered trash receptacle in the women's restroom.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 What appeared to be spilled soda syrup was observed on the floor at the west end of the main floor bar. Buildup was observed along the back wall of the bar under the ice bin. Manager believed this could be due to lines being changed by the company that came out for service as there did not appear to be a current leak. The floor will be cleaned later today.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Floor of the large walk-in cooler was observed with chipped flooring near the door and in a few spots within the cooler. Repair the floor in the walk-in cooler.
-Small holes were observed in the walls of the restrooms where old dispensers were removed. Seal the holes.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-303.11 Light fixture closest to the entrance of the men’s restroom on the second floor was not working. At least one light bulb was burnt out while another was missing. Provide lighting in the front restroom fixture. 
Light intensity shall be at least 20 foot candles (215 lux) in restrooms.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Ice bins at the main bar were observed to have a paper clip in the bottom of one and debris in the bottom of the other. Management and owner were made area of the physical contamination. Both ice bins were to be properly cleaned and sanitized prior to opening later this afternoon.

Soda guns at the upstairs bar were soaking in what appeared to be sanitizer solution (blue color to the solution/partially undissolved tablets). One pitcher had gritty debris and what appeared to be part of a blue cleaning towel in the solution as well. Solutions were emptied. Proper cleaning and sanitizing of soda guns was discussed. All soda guns and nozzles were to be properly cleaned and sanitized prior to opening later this afternoon.

Ice in both ice machines was observed to have what appeared to be mold in it. The larger ice machine had one piece of ice that looked questionable, which was removed from the machine. The smaller machine had several pieces that had mold on/in them. The baffle inside the machine was observed with mold buildup, and condensation was dripping off the mold onto the ice. The smaller machine was turned off to be cleaned and sanitized by staff. A call for service will be made to the technician who services and does detail cleaning/switching of filters. Management and owner were advised as to the cleaning and sanitizing responsibilities of staff between detail service from contracted technician. 

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A rather long screw was observed sticking halfway inside the ice bin by the handsink at the main bar. Screw was used to attach the speed rail to the bin. The screw appeared to have the start of rust formation, and is a safety hazard. Management and owner will work to make proper repairs.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
(R) 750.690 - Legs of both ice machines were held up by unsealed wood and cardboard. The material used to hold up the legs is getting worn and soiled with mold/splash. Replace the items used for leveling the ice machine and use materials that are smooth and easily cleanable, such as sealed cinder blocks or painted/sealed wood.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.citation_text:
750.1030 - Cold water was initially off at the right handsink in the women's room on the main floor. Water was turned on during the inspection.

Water under pressure at the required temperature shall be provided to all fixtures and equipment that use water.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Mopsink was observed to be heavily soiled and slow draining. Clean the mopsink and call a plumber for service if staff are unable to alleviate the issue with available products at the facility.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - Basement floor was a significant crack in the middle between the two ice machine. Also the floor under the ice machines was soiled with general buildup/debris.
Clean the floor and provide proper repairs so the basement floor is sealed and easy to clean/maintain clean.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
